title: Consumption signature merge & metering fallback worker
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a resilient reconciliation worker that merges per-request consumption signatures (streaming token attributions) into the canonical billing ledger while providing deterministic fallback behavior when provenance telemetry is partial or delayed. This job sits between the streaming token capture (kafka topic: tokens.provenance) and the billing compactor. Primary goals: 1) ensure idempotent ledger writes for duplicates or replays, 2) provide a deterministic fallback path that attributes usage using route heuristics when signatures are missing, 3) keep tail-latency and cost of the pipeline acceptable, and 4) enable backfill and delta-merge operations for historical corrections.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Worker consumes from tokens.provenance and tokens.missing repair topic, producing canonical ledger writes with at-most-once semantics into billing.outgoing (validated by token hash and event_id). 2) Fallback attribution uses last-known-route mapping + model-family heuristics and marks records with provenance_reason: 'fallback-heuristic' for downstream auditing. 3) End-to-end latency for reconciled records < 90s for 95th percentile under normal load. 4) Comprehensive unit + integration tests, and a staged rollout with feature-flag. 5) Backfill tool can re-run deltas for a given window and annotate corrections.
notes:
Design tradeoffs: prefer idempotent writes keyed by (customer_id, request_fingerprint, ingest_window) to avoid complex two-phase commits. Chosen storage backend for interim dedupe is RocksDB-backed local state for Kafka Streams; long-term canonical store remains BigQuery for batch queries and a compacted PostgreSQL ledger for low-latency reads. We must limit memory pressure by sharding keys and TTL-ing state after ledger ack.
Observability: expose per-customer reconciliation lag, fallback-rate, duplicate-detection-rate, and last-corrected-window on the Console billing dashboard.
Rollout plan: internal canary on 5 small customers -> expand to dedicated customers -> enable default for hosted after 72h stability window.
Backfill approach: run delta-merge job that computes signature diffs and emits corrective ledger entries with a correction_tag and provenance anchor.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Initial design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Consumption+Signature+Merge - feedback requested from Billing and Platform

2026-02-22 - Architecture review: decided on Kafka Streams worker with RocksDB local state for dedupe. Highlight: avoid cross-partition join for performance. Action: Diego to prototype local state size estimation.
2026-02-28 - Prototype results: local RocksDB footprint ~120MB per shard for 30-day window; dedupe throughput ~10k events/s per vCPU. Filed follow-up ENG-69610 for optimized compaction strategy.

2026-03-04 - Security review kickoff: need to ensure PII never lands in intermediate topics; use tokenized identifiers and KMS envelope encryption for payloads. Link to checklist: https://vault.redwood.ai/sso/billing-security-checklist

2026-03-09 - Integration test PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1427 (work-in-progress) - unit tests green, flakey integration test on CI related to race during compactor ACKs
2026-03-12 - Observability hooks added to instrumentation library; dashboard draft: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/billing/reconciler-lag (internal)
implementation_notes:
- Worker language: Go (match existing streaming infra)
- Consumer group per-deployment region to keep routing deterministic
- Use feature-flag 'reconciler.v1.enable_fallback' for controlled enablement
- Persist corrective entries with correction_tag and original_event_id to aid audits
- Support dry-run mode that writes to billing.audit for validation before ledger commits
